not_worst_case_because: the LM393 publishes no maximum response time at all -- 1.3 us is a typical at 5 mV overdrive, and the datasheet itself shows the figure rising as overdrive falls, so a slow part lengthens every total
the CD4013 stage is a max (400 ns), but only at VDD = 5 V and 25 C with a 20 ns input edge; it is not a max over the full temperature range at this board's edge rate

the UCC27524A's switching parameters are not tested in production (the datasheet says so itself), and its 13/23 ns are specified at VDD = 12 V, CLOAD = 1.8 nF and 125 C, not over the part-to-part spread
the eight 200 k pull-ups that set the permit rail's ceiling are a typical with no published min or max, so the 0.26 V ceiling is a nominal figure rather than a guaranteed bound
the gate fall omits the driver's internal sink resistance, which adds time

the comparator's 1.3 us was measured through a 5.1 k pull-up and 15 pF; this board uses 10 k, and the added time constant scales with the load capacitance, which is not measured -- the priced 73.5 ns is what the datasheet's own C_L produces, not what this layout produces
no temperature or device spread is applied: every value is a nominal part-table arithmetic, not a worst-case-over-temperature figure

detection.note: the deck runs the real RC network, so the pole constants are already inside these two numbers; adding them again would double-count 47 us and 75 us

comparator.source: references/datasheets/lm393.txt (SLCS005AH, revised April 2025; section 5.11 Switching Characteristics)
comparator.conditions: VCC = 5 V, TA = 25 C, RL 5.1 k to 5 V, CL = 15 pF; the cited value is the 100 mV step with 5 mV overdrive, and the interval ends when the output crosses 1.4 V
comparator.reason_typ_only: section 5.11 has a TYP column and no MAX for the non-B part, so a slower comparator makes every total longer than this floor

latch.source: references/datasheets/cd4013b.txt (SCHS023E, revised September 2016; section 6.6 Electrical Characteristics: Dynamic, VDD = 5 V)
latch.wiring: FF1 on this board: SET = FLT, RESET = RST_EFF, clock and D tied off, and ~Q is the permit term
latch.conditions: VDD = 5 V, TA = 25 C, CL = 50 pF, RL = 20 k, input tr/tf = 20 ns

permit_release.sr_driver_release_reason: the UCC27524A's EN pin capacitance is unpublished, so the 1 nF counted here is C28 only and extra pin capacitance only lengthens the fall; the eight EN pins do reach this node directly

driver_disable.ucc27524a_source: references/datasheets/ucc27524a.txt (SLUSBP4C, revised June 2024; ENABLE and Switching Characteristics tables, Device Logic Table 6-2)
driver_disable.ucc27524a_package: D (SOIC-8), the UCC27524ADR on this board
driver_disable.ucc27524a_output_state_reason: Device Logic Table 6-2 drives OUTA/OUTB low whenever the matching ENx is low, and the tD4x condition -- VENx_L of the enable fall to 90% of output fall -- describes a driven edge, not a floating pin; so the SR gate keeps its 2.2 ohm path and the 110.9 us dead-driver figure does not apply to a released permit rail

sr.with_driver_omits: the driver's internal sink resistance: the vendored UCC27282 text names RHOL/RLOL but publishes no value
sr.pulldown_only_omits: nothing but the detector branch, which is a DC path to ground as well; the diode drop only shortens the exponent's effective start

primary.with_driver_omits: the driver's internal sink resistance: the vendored UCC27282 text names RHOL/RLOL but publishes no value
primary.pulldown_only_omits: nothing but the detector branch, which is a DC path to ground as well; the diode drop only shortens the exponent's effective start
